newsitem.title: USA: California counties to join suit over "Joe Camel" ads.
newsitem.headline: California counties to join suit over "Joe Camel" ads.

text.p: Eleven California counties and the city of San Jose said Thursday they would join a lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., challenging "Joe Camel" advertising that allegedly targets children.
The lawsuit seeks an injunction, in addition to civil penalties and the refund of profits from R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.

If the lawsuit is successful, attorneys for the California governments said R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. could be forced to turn over hundreds of millions of dollars in profits from sales generated by the controversial advertising campaign.
"I can't put Joe Camel's creators in jail," said San Francisco's attorney, Louise Renne. "But I can lighten their wallets."

Renne told reporters that the 11 California counties, including San Francisco, and the city of San Jose filed a joint motion on Thursday in state Superior Court to join the 1991 Mangini lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco and the advertising agency Mezzina Brown Inc.

The court has to approve the motion, which is expected to face opposition. The case is set for trial on Dec. 8, 1997. Assuming no delays, it would be the first major tobacco lawsuit to go to court trial in the state.
"The evidence will show that they knowingly sought to target young people," Renne said. "We are out to stop that."

The lawsuit alleges that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco's "Joe Camel" campaign "aids and abets" the violation of state law because it is illegal to sell cigarettes to minors, San Francisco attorney Elizabeth Laporte said.
"It (Joe Camel) encourages them (minors) to violate the law and it encourages retailers to violate the law," plaintiffs' attorney Alan Caplan said.
A spokeswoman for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco said the company's attorneys have not seen a copy of San Francisco's motion and could not at this time comment on it.
Spokeswoman Peggy Carter said, however, that the "Joe Camel" campaign does not target children.
"Kids should not be smoking, and we have programs out there in the schools and for parents to help be part of the solution to reduce youth smoking," she said.

Earlier this week, a Federal Trade Commission spokesperson said staff members have asked the commissioners to act against R.J. Reynolds because new evidence shows the tobacco company's "Joe Camel" campaign targets children.
The "Joe Camel" lawsuit in California will be the third filed by San Francisco and the other local governments. They have already filed suits against tobacco companies in federal and state court.
"We are now on a three course path," Renne said. "We are not going away."
The counties have been in contact with officials representing Liggett Group. "They indicated a willingness to help us" in the "Joe Camel" lawsuit, plaintiffs' attorney Patrick Coughlin said.

Earlier this month, Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd., broke ranks with other tobacco companies by agreeing to settle with 22 state attorneys general who sued the industry to recoup smoking-related Medicaid health care costs.
The state of California, the most populous state, with potentially billions of dollars in claims, has so far not sued the tobacco industry.
